Commands outside uv pip ignore [pip] ("These values will be ignored when running commands outside the `uv pip` namespace", PipOptions in crates/uv-settings/src/settings.rs). keys maps each top-level key depcurfew writes to the [pip] key that overrides or extends it. The same code in 0.11.32 (crates/uv/src/settings.rs). [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/0.13.6/crates/uv-cli/src/settings.rs)

### pip

- `cooldown.setting`: Only files uploaded before the given time are considered; applies to packages from remote indexes, not to local files, find-links directories or VCS requirements. Isolated build environments get the same cutoff. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/docs/html/user_guide.rst#filtering-by-upload-time)
- `cooldown.configFiles`: pip reads no configuration from the project: only the global, user and site (virtual environment) pip.conf, the file named by PIP_CONFIG_FILE and PIP_* environment variables. --uploaded-prior-to is not allowed in requirements files, so a project sets it through PIP_UPLOADED_PRIOR_TO or the command line, e.g. in CI. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/docs/html/topics/configuration.md)
- `cooldown.cliFlag`: pip install, download, wheel, lock, index and list; environment variable PIP_UPLOADED_PRIOR_TO. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/docs/html/user_guide.rst#filtering-by-upload-time)
- `cooldown.unit`: A duration is written PnD, a whole number of days (P3D, matched by ^P(\d+)D$); P1W, PT24H and "7 days" are rejected. An ISO 8601 date or time is a fixed cutoff instead. A day is always 24 hours. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/src/pip/_internal/cli/cmdoptions.py)
- `cooldown.availableSince`: pip 26.1 accepts a duration in days ("P3D for 3 days ago"); the option itself exists since 26.0 with dates only. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/NEWS.rst)
- `cooldown.default`: Off unless given. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/docs/html/user_guide.rst#filtering-by-upload-time)
- `installScripts.defaultPolicy`: pip builds a source distribution when no wheel fits, which runs its build backend; the secure-installs guide recommends --only-binary :all:. Installing a wheel runs no package code. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/docs/html/topics/secure-installs.md)
- `installScripts.allowList.setting`: After --only-binary=:all:, a package named in --no-binary may only be installed from source: a name wins over :all:, so its wheels are not used. --only-binary=:all: given after it clears the exception. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/src/pip/_internal/models/format_control.py)
- `installScripts.allowList.file`: --only-binary and --no-binary are among the options a requirements file may contain. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/src/pip/_internal/req/req_file.py)
- `installScripts.allowList.format`: Each use adds to the set; :all: and :none: are special values. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/src/pip/_internal/cli/cmdoptions.py)
- `installScripts.disableAll`: Allowed in requirements files and pip.conf (only-binary). Enforced only for packages from indexes and find-links: VCS, local directory and direct URL source requirements are still built. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/docs/html/topics/secure-installs.md)
- `project.lockfiles`: pip lock (experimental since 25.1) writes pylock.toml; pip install -r pylock.toml is experimental since 26.1. The specification also allows pylock.<name>.toml (extra.lockfilePattern). [↗](https://github.com/pypa/packaging.python.org/blob/6fa4790c1fb668830f6eb94bbfe832320a9b0a2b/source/specifications/pylock-toml.rst#file-name)
- `project.manifests`: "requirements.txt is usually what these files are named (although, that is not a requirement)"; the format is meant only for pip. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/docs/html/reference/requirements-file-format.md)
- `user.files`: The user file is pip.conf (pip.ini on Windows) in appdirs.user_config_dir("pip") (configuration.py), written in INI with [global] and per-command sections. Linux: $HOME/.config/pip/pip.conf, "which respects the XDG_CONFIG_HOME environment variable" (used when it is not empty after stripping spaces, vendored platformdirs _xdg.py). macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/pip when that directory exists, else ~/.config/pip, where XDG_CONFIG_HOME is not used (utils/appdirs.py: _macos_user_config_dir takes platformdirs user_data_dir when os.path.isdir); since 26.2 that user_data_dir is $XDG_DATA_HOME/pip when XDG_DATA_HOME is not empty after stripping spaces, so with XDG_DATA_HOME set the Library directory is skipped and ~/.config/pip is used unless $XDG_DATA_HOME/pip exists (XDGMixin in src/pip/_vendor/platformdirs/_xdg.py at 26.2.2; src/pip/_vendor/vendor.txt names platformdirs 4.10.0 in 26.2 and 4.5.1 in 26.1.1, whose macos.py has no XDG handling). Windows: %APPDATA%\pip\pip.ini; platformdirs asks Windows for the Roaming AppData known folder, which APPDATA normally names. The legacy ~/.pip/pip.conf (%HOME%\pip\pip.ini) is loaded as well, below this file. Same path code in 25.0; earlier versions are not tracked. A command reads [global] and the section named after itself, which wins key by key (override_order ["global", self.name, ":env:"] in cli/parser.py); the options doctor --user checks (index_group and package_selection_group in cli/cmdoptions.py) belong to install, download, wheel, lock, index and list (src/pip/_internal/commands at 26.2.2). Keys are read without regard to case and with underscores as dashes, so only_binary in a file is the same setting as only-binary, and the later one wins (_normalize_name in src/pip/_internal/configuration.py at 26.2.2: name.lower().replace("_", "-"), applied to every key of every file). [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/docs/html/topics/configuration.md#location)
- `user.settings`: depcurfew writes them in [global], which reaches every command that has the option (install, download, wheel, lock, index, list) and the resolver of pipenv lock; [install] reaches only pip install. "Accept --no-binary and --only-binary via pip.conf" (7.1.0); uploaded-prior-to is read from pip.conf like every long option ("To override a duration set in configuration, pass P0D on the command line", user_guide.rst). 26.1.0 because depcurfew writes a PnD duration: pip 26.0 takes dates only and aborts on P7D, and 25.x ignores the key. uv does not read pip.conf. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/NEWS.rst)
- `user.unknownKeys`: "Ignore options not present in this parser": a key that is not an option of the command is skipped without a word (same code in 25.0), so pip before 26.0 ignores uploaded-prior-to. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/src/pip/_internal/cli/parser.py)
- `user.invalidValueFails`: A pip.conf that is not valid INI stops pip (ConfigurationFileCouldNotBeLoaded, configuration.py), and a value an option rejects ends the command with a usage error: pip 26.0 aborts on uploaded-prior-to = P7D in every command that has the option, as it rejected PIP_UPLOADED_PRIOR_TO=P100000D in a test on 2026-10-30 (configuration values and PIP_* variables go through the same parsing). Commands without the option ignore the key. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/src/pip/_internal/cli/parser.py)
- `user.weakening`: In any section of any pip.conf: [install] beats [global], and a later file (a virtual environment pip.conf, PIP_CONFIG_FILE) beats the user file per key, an empty value removing it (cli/parser.py). :all: in one of the lists clears the other and :none: clears its own (handle_mutual_excludes). P0D overrides a configured duration, and "Local package files are allowed regardless of the --uploaded-prior-to setting", find-links directories included (user_guide.rst). A requirements file can also pass --no-binary or --only-binary, but not --uploaded-prior-to. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/src/pip/_internal/models/format_control.py)
- `user.variables`: "Note that if a file exists at the location that this is set to, the user config file will not be loaded." PIP_<NAME> variables are applied after the [global] and command sections of all files, and the command line beats them (cli/parser.py, override_order). --isolated, a flag, ignores environment variables and user configuration. XDG_CONFIG_HOME (Linux) and XDG_DATA_HOME (macOS, 26.2) move the user directory (see files). [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/docs/html/topics/configuration.md)
- `extra.configSections`: "Each subcommand can be configured optionally in its own section. This overrides the global setting with the same name", and "A command specific section in the config file `[<command>] host = bar` overrides the option with same name in the `[global]` config file section" (Precedence / Override order). pip reads only [global], the section of the running command and :env: (override_order = ["global", self.name, ":env:"] in cli/parser.py), so a managed key in [install] wins over [global] for pip install; depcurfew comments such keys out in every section other than [global]. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/docs/html/topics/configuration.md)
- `extra.pylockCreatedBy`: pip lock writes created-by = "pip". [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/src/pip/_internal/utils/pylock.py)
- `extra.requirementsOptions`: SUPPORTED_OPTIONS in pip 26.2.2 (--pypi-url is a second name of --index-url in cmdoptions.py); per requirement also --hash and -C/--config-settings (extra.requirementsParser). Any other option, --uploaded-prior-to included, makes the file fail to parse. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/src/pip/_internal/req/req_file.py)
- `extra.requirementsParser`: build_parser reads each line with optparse.OptionParser(add_help_option=False) holding SUPPORTED_OPTIONS and SUPPORTED_OPTIONS_REQ (--hash, -C/--config-settings), with the names from cmdoptions.py in pip 26.2.2. optparse takes a long option shortened to a prefix that names exactly one of them (_match_abbrev; an exact name wins), so --no-bin :all: is --no-binary :all:, and an ambiguous prefix such as --no is an error. --hash and --config-settings belong to the requirement on their line; on a line of their own they are accepted and ignored. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/src/pip/_internal/req/req_file.py)
- `extra.configFileNames`: CONFIG_BASENAME is pip.ini on Windows and pip.conf elsewhere; pip looks for it only in the global, user and site locations, never in the project. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/src/pip/_internal/configuration.py)
- `extra.configFileVariable`: Names a configuration file pip loads last; set to os.devnull it turns all configuration files off. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/docs/html/topics/configuration.md#environment-variable)
- `extra.environmentVariable`: Every long option has a PIP_<UPPER_LONG_NAME> variable with dashes replaced by underscores. Tested on 2026-10-30: pip 25.3 ignored PIP_UPLOADED_PRIOR_TO=P100000D without a word, 26.0 rejected the duration (dates only), 26.1 and 26.2.2 found no version. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/docs/html/topics/configuration.md#environment-variables)
- `extra.durationStrings`: Only whole days, written PnD, are accepted. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/NEWS.rst)
- `extra.missingUploadTime`: Upload times exist only in the JSON form of the simple repository API (PEP 700); indexes that serve only HTML have none. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/docs/html/user_guide.rst#filtering-by-upload-time)
- `extra.lockfileFormat`: Each [[packages]] entry has exactly one of vcs (always built), directory (always built), archive (a source tree or wheel at a URL or path) or sdist and wheels from an index. A package with an sdist and no wheels is built when installed. A relative directory path is relative to the lock file. The required top-level created-by records the name of the tool that wrote the file, preferably its normalized Python package name. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/packaging.python.org/blob/6fa4790c1fb668830f6eb94bbfe832320a9b0a2b/source/specifications/pylock-toml.rst)
- `extra.requirementsFormat`: VCS requirements start with git+, hg+, svn+ or bzr+, alone or after "name @"; a direct reference is "name @ URL" (PEP 508); -e installs a project path or VCS URL in editable mode. The legacy #egg= fragment names the project of a VCS URL. Lines ending with a backslash continue on the next line, and # starts a comment (requirements-file-format.md). [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/docs/html/topics/vcs-support.md)
- `extra.requirementsIncludes`: Option names from cli/cmdoptions.py. A relative path is relative to the directory of the file that includes it, and a file given as an http, https or file URL is downloaded (req_file.py, _parse_and_recurse); a file that includes itself is an error. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/docs/html/reference/requirements-file-format.md#referring-to-other-requirements-files)
- `extra.requirementsPaths`: A requirement that contains a path separator (/, and \ on Windows) or starts with . looks like a path (_looks_like_path): a directory there is a project built from source. A name with an archive extension (utils/filetypes.py) is a local archive, even when the file does not exist. http, https, ftp and file URLs are links (utils/urls.py, is_url). [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/src/pip/_internal/req/constructors.py)
- `extra.lockfilePattern`: A named lock file, next to or instead of pylock.toml; pip lock -o writes any name. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/packaging.python.org/blob/6fa4790c1fb668830f6eb94bbfe832320a9b0a2b/source/specifications/pylock-toml.rst#file-name)
- `extra.commandLine`: pip and pip3 are the console scripts of the package (pyproject.toml). The options of pip install (install.py) and the general options of every command (cmdoptions.py, general_group), which may also come before install. pip reads them with optparse: --opt value and --opt=value, -rFILE and -r FILE, grouped short flags, and a long option shortened to any prefix that names one option (cli/parser.py keeps optparse's matching), so --extra means --extra-index-url. -e takes a local project path or a VCS URL to install in editable mode. -r, -c, --requirements-from-script and --group read requirements from files of the project. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/src/pip/_internal/commands/install.py)
- `extra.registryOverrides`: index_group: --index-url (alias -i, --pypi-url) is the base URL of the package index, --extra-index-url adds indexes, --find-links (-f) adds an HTML page or a directory of archives. Every long option can be set as PIP_<UPPER_LONG_NAME>, dashes replaced by underscores (docs/html/topics/configuration.md); PIP_CONFIG_FILE names a configuration file loaded last, which may set any index. Requirements files may set --index-url, --extra-index-url and --find-links too (req/req_file.py). [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/src/pip/_internal/cli/cmdoptions.py)
- `extra.selection`: --pre includes pre-release and development versions (pip only finds stable versions by default) and stands for --all-releases :all:; --all-releases and --only-final take :all:, :none: or package names separated by commas and allow or forbid pre-releases of those packages (models/release_control.py, allows_prereleases: a named package first, then :all:). --no-binary and --only-binary take the same lists: --no-binary keeps pip from using wheels, so the package is built from source, --only-binary from using source distributions (models/format_control.py, handle_mutual_excludes and get_allowed_formats). Each long option can also be set as PIP_<NAME> (docs/html/topics/configuration.md), which the command line overrides. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/src/pip/_internal/cli/cmdoptions.py)
- `extra.pipxSelection`: pipx forwards the standard PIP_* variables to pip (except PIP_USER, PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK, PIP_TARGET and PIP_KEYRING_PROVIDER); the uv backend ignores them (docs/how-to/use-private-index.rst). pipx has no option of its own for pre-releases or source builds; --pip-args may carry them. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/1.18.10/docs/reference/environment-variables.rst)
- `extra.pipxCommandLine`: pipx installs applications from PyPI with pip (or uv) in environments of their own. pipx install takes one or more package specs, a VCS URL, a local path or archive, or a script (--preinstall adds packages to the environment; -f is --force, not find-links). pipx run takes the app first (argparse REMAINDER, so its options come before it), --spec names the package to install and run, --with adds packages; a first argument ending in .py is a local script, or a script to download when it is a URL (docs/how-to/run-scripts.rst). argparse accepts abbreviated long options. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/1.18.10/src/pipx/main.py)
- `extra.pipxRegistryOverrides`: --index-url is the base URL of the index; --pip-args is split and handed to pip, so it may carry --extra-index-url, --find-links or --no-index. With the pip backend pipx passes the PIP_* variables on to pip; with the uv backend it ignores them and uv reads its own (docs/how-to/use-uv-backend.rst); both kinds are registry variables of pip and uv. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/1.18.10/src/pipx/main.py)
- `extra.latestVersion`: Released on 2026-10-20. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/NEWS.rst)

### Poetry

- `cooldown.setting`: A version is ignored while any of its files was uploaded less than the given number of days ago. Applies when dependencies are resolved (poetry lock, add, update); poetry install installs the locked versions without checking. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/docs/configuration.md#solvermin-release-age)
- `cooldown.configFiles`: The local configuration next to pyproject.toml (poetry config --local), not pyproject.toml itself. Environment variables (POETRY_SOLVER_MIN_RELEASE_AGE) win over poetry.toml, which wins over the user config.toml. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/docs/configuration.md#local-configuration)
- `cooldown.unit`: An integer; 0 (the default) turns it off. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/docs/configuration.md#solvermin-release-age)
- `cooldown.availableSince`: "Introduced in 2.4.0"; announced as dependency cooldowns. Tested on 2026-10-30: Poetry 2.3.4 locked with min-release-age = 100000 in poetry.toml without a word, while 2.4.0 and 2.5.1 found no version. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/docs/configuration.md#solvermin-release-age)
- `cooldown.default`: Default 0: all versions are considered. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/docs/configuration.md#solvermin-release-age)
- `installScripts.defaultPolicy`: Without installer.only-binary, packages are built from source distributions when no wheel fits, which runs their build backend. Git and directory dependencies are always built. Installing a wheel runs no package code. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/docs/configuration.md#installeronly-binary)
- `installScripts.allowList.setting`: With installer.only-binary = [":all:"], the packages named in installer.no-binary are the only ones built from source; explicit names take precedence over :all: since 2.2.0. Their wheels are rejected, so they are always built. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/src/poetry/installation/chooser.py)
- `installScripts.allowList.file`: The docs recommend configuring it with --local for a project. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/docs/configuration.md#installerno-binary)
- `installScripts.allowList.availableSince`: "explicit package names will take precedence over :all:" (#10278). Before 2.2.0 a package listed in both settings has no file left to install. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/CHANGELOG.md)
- `installScripts.allowList.format`: poetry config stores the value as a list; written by hand, a boolean is not normalized. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/docs/configuration.md#installerno-binary)
- `installScripts.disableAll`: Since 2.0.0; the value [":all:"] forbids source distributions for every package. Applied only when installing: resolving dependencies may still build source distributions without static metadata, and git, path and url dependencies are built regardless. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/docs/configuration.md#installeronly-binary)
- `project.lockfiles`: Next to pyproject.toml. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/src/poetry/factory.py)
- `user.settings`: Every setting of Config.default_config is read from the user config.toml ("As with all configurations described here, this is a user specific configuration", docs/configuration.md); dotted names are nested tables. A project poetry.toml replaces a user value, lists included (merge_dicts in src/poetry/utils/helpers.py), and POETRY_* variables beat both. Names in installer.no-binary win over installer.only-binary = :all: only since 2.2.0. solver.min-release-age-exclude is written as a TOML array (see extra.excludeFormat). [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/src/poetry/config/config.py)
- `user.weakening`: Precedence: environment variables, then the local poetry.toml, then the global config.toml, then the default; a poetry.toml key replaces the user value, lists included. solver.min-release-age-exclude-source (2.4.0) takes source names from pyproject.toml or URLs. A source that gives no upload times is not filtered at all. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/docs/configuration.md#configuration-sources)
- `user.variables`: Any setting can be set as POETRY_ plus its name in capitals with dots and dashes replaced by underscores, and environment variables come first in the precedence ("Configuration sources"). POETRY_CONFIG_DIR replaces the platform directory (src/poetry/locations.py). [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/docs/configuration.md#using-environment-variables)
- `extra.pylockCreatedBy`: Poetry exports pylock.toml with its export plugin (poetry export --format pylock.toml), which writes created-by = "poetry-plugin-export". [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry-plugin-export/blob/1.10.1/src/poetry_plugin_export/exporter.py)
- `extra.configTable`: poetry config writes dotted settings as nested tables, e.g. [solver] min-release-age = 7. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/src/poetry/config/file_config_source.py)
- `extra.pyprojectTable`: A [tool.poetry] table marks a Poetry project; Poetry also accepts a [project] table with a static name and version, which other tools use as well. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry-core/blob/2.5.0/src/poetry/core/pyproject/toml.py)
- `extra.buildSwitch`: installer.only-binary was added in 2.0.0; [":all:"] forbids source distributions of index packages when installing. Git and directory dependencies, and source archives from a URL or path, are built regardless (src/poetry/installation/executor.py at 2.5.1). [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/CHANGELOG.md)
- `extra.excludeWildcards`: Package names only. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/docs/configuration.md#solvermin-release-age-exclude)
- `extra.requiredVersion`: A version constraint in pyproject.toml; a Poetry version outside it raises an error. Poetry 1.x does not know the key. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/docs/pyproject.md#requires-poetry)
- `extra.commandLine`: poetry add takes package specs: a name, name@constraint, a PEP 508 requirement, a git URL, a path or an archive URL. Options with a value: --group (-G), --extras (-E), --optional, --python, --platform, --markers and --source of add, and the global --directory (-C) and --project (-P); -e/--editable, -D/--dev, --allow-prereleases, --dry-run and --lock are flags (src/poetry/console/commands/add.py). cleo reads -Gdocs and -G docs; long options cannot be shortened. poetry install takes no package specs. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/docs/cli.md#add)
- `extra.registryOverrides`: --source names a package source of [[tool.poetry.source]] in pyproject.toml (or pypi) to take the package from. The POETRY_REPOSITORIES_<NAME>_URL variables are for publishing only; no variable sets a package source. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/docs/repositories.md)
- `extra.versionConstraints`: poetry add name@constraint takes any constraint valid in pyproject.toml, and name@latest the newest release; extras go before the @ (name[extra]@^4.0.0). ^ keeps the left-most non-zero part of major.minor.patch: ^1.2.3 is >=1.2.3 <2.0.0, ^1.2 is >=1.2.0 <2.0.0, ^1 is >=1.0.0 <2.0.0, ^0.2.3 is >=0.2.3 <0.3.0, ^0.0.3 is >=0.0.3 <0.0.4, ^0.0 is >=0.0.0 <0.1.0, ^0 is >=0.0.0 <1.0.0. ~ allows patch changes, or minor changes when only a major version is given: ~1.2.3 is >=1.2.3 <1.3.0, ~1.2 is >=1.2.0 <1.3.0, ~1 is >=1.0.0 <2.0.0. * is any version, 1.* is >=1.0.0 <2.0.0, 1.2.* is >=1.2.0 <1.3.0. ~=, inequalities and == as in PEP 440, several separated by commas; a bare version (1.2.3) is that version only. Poetry prefers stable releases and takes a pre-release only when no stable release satisfies the constraint. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/docs/dependency-specification.md#using-the--operator)
- `extra.selection`: installer.no-binary (POETRY_INSTALLER_NO_BINARY) disallows wheels for :all: or true, none for :none: or false, or the named packages separated by commas; installer.only-binary (POETRY_INSTALLER_ONLY_BINARY, since 2.0.0) takes the same values; explicit package names win over :all:. poetry add --allow-prereleases accepts pre-releases (src/poetry/console/commands/add.py). [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/docs/configuration.md)
- `extra.latestVersion`: Released on 2026-09-20. [↗](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/CHANGELOG.md)

### PDM

- `cooldown.setting`: In the [tool.pdm.resolution] table of pyproject.toml: distributions uploaded after the cutoff are left out when dependencies are resolved (pdm lock, add, update). The --exclude-newer option of pdm lock wins over it, and it wins over strategy.exclude-newer in the PDM configuration. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/docs/usage/lockfile.md#exclude-packages-newer-than-specific-date)
- `cooldown.configFiles`: The [tool.pdm.resolution] table. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/docs/usage/lockfile.md#exclude-packages-newer-than-specific-date)
- `cooldown.cliFlag`: pdm lock --exclude-newer, since 2.13.0. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/docs/usage/lockfile.md#exclude-packages-newer-than-specific-date)
- `cooldown.unit`: An RFC 3339 timestamp, a UTC date or a relative duration N{d|h|w} such as 7d, 12h or 3w, counted from the current UTC time. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/docs/usage/lockfile.md#exclude-packages-newer-than-specific-date)
- `cooldown.availableSince`: "Support exclude-newer in pyproject.toml in the [tool.pdm.resolution] table" (#3776); the pdm lock option exists since 2.13.0. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/CHANGELOG.md)
- `cooldown.default`: No default: without a value every upload time is accepted. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/docs/usage/lockfile.md#exclude-packages-newer-than-specific-date)
- `cooldown.exclude.setting`: A table [tool.pdm.resolution.exclude-newer-override] of package = false (no cutoff) or package = another date or duration; package-specific values win over the global cutoff. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/docs/usage/lockfile.md#exclude-packages-newer-than-specific-date)
- `cooldown.exclude.availableSince`: "Allow package-specific overrides for exclude-newer resolution limits" (#3809). [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/CHANGELOG.md)
- `installScripts.defaultPolicy`: Without only-binary, PDM locks and installs source distributions when they fit, which builds them and runs their build backend. Installing a wheel runs no package code. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/docs/usage/lockfile.md#set-acceptable-format-for-locking-or-installing)
- `installScripts.allowList.setting`: The packages in no-binary are locked and installed from source distributions only. A name in no-binary wins over only-binary = ":all:" (FormatControl of unearth, which PDM uses), so with both the named packages are the only ones built, and always from source. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/docs/usage/lockfile.md#set-acceptable-format-for-locking-or-installing)
- `installScripts.allowList.file`: The [tool.pdm.resolution] table. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/docs/usage/lockfile.md#set-acceptable-format-for-locking-or-installing)
- `installScripts.allowList.availableSince`: no-binary, only-binary and prefer-binary keys in [tool.pdm.resolution] (#2656). [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/CHANGELOG.md)
- `installScripts.disableAll`: only-binary = ":all:" locks and installs only wheels. The variables PDM_ONLY_BINARY and PDM_NO_BINARY win over pyproject.toml. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/docs/usage/lockfile.md#set-acceptable-format-for-locking-or-installing)
- `project.lockfiles`: pdm.lock next to pyproject.toml; pdm lock --lockfile writes another name. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/docs/usage/lockfile.md)
- `user.settings`: "Allow configuring the default lock --exclude-newer value with strategy.exclude-newer" (2.27.0, #3795): a TOML string such as "7d", a date or an RFC 3339 time. It applies where neither [tool.pdm.resolution] exclude-newer in pyproject.toml nor a project pdm.toml sets it (docs/usage/lockfile.md), and with it in effect pdm lock resolves every package again (src/pdm/cli/commands/lock.py). only-binary, no-binary and exclude-newer-override cannot be set in any PDM configuration file: PDM reads them from [tool.pdm.resolution] in pyproject.toml, only-binary and no-binary also from PDM_ONLY_BINARY and PDM_NO_BINARY (environments/base.py, Project.env_or_setting), so at user level they can be set only through those variables. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/CHANGELOG.md)
- `user.weakening`: use_uv (experimental since 2.19.0, PDM_USE_UV) can be set in config.toml and in a project pdm.toml, which wins. PDM passes the cutoff and the build settings to uv lock but not to uv sync --frozen (src/pdm/installers/uv.py), and passes no --no-config, so uv also reads the user uv.toml. A home strategy.exclude-newer cannot weaken a project that sets [tool.pdm.resolution] exclude-newer. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/docs/usage/uv.md)
- `user.variables`: env_or_setting returns os.getenv(var) or the pyproject.toml setting, so a non-empty PDM_ONLY_BINARY or PDM_NO_BINARY wins (environments/base.py). -c/--config and PDM_CONFIG_FILE name the home config file (src/pdm/core.py). PDM_USE_UV is the variable of use_uv, and variables beat pdm.toml and config.toml (src/pdm/project/config.py). [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/src/pdm/project/core.py)
- `extra.pylockCreatedBy`: PDM's pylock.toml export writes created-by = "pdm". [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/src/pdm/formats/pylock.py)
- `extra.configTables`: exclude-newer, its overrides, only-binary and no-binary share the table. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/docs/usage/lockfile.md#exclude-packages-newer-than-specific-date)
- `extra.pyprojectTable`: PDM keeps its settings in [tool.pdm] of pyproject.toml. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/docs/reference/pep621.md)
- `extra.buildSwitch`: only-binary in [tool.pdm.resolution] since 2.15.0 (#2656). It covers packages from an index: git, URL and path requirements already name their source and are built regardless (candidates.py). [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/CHANGELOG.md)
- `extra.durationStrings`: "pdm lock --exclude-newer now accepts relative durations in the format N{d|h|w}" (#3760). [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/CHANGELOG.md)
- `extra.durationUnits`: Written as Nh, Nd and Nw. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/docs/usage/lockfile.md#exclude-packages-newer-than-specific-date)
- `extra.excludeWildcards`: Override keys are package names. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/docs/usage/lockfile.md#exclude-packages-newer-than-specific-date)
- `extra.excludeValue`: package = false disables the cutoff for that package. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/docs/usage/lockfile.md#exclude-packages-newer-than-specific-date)
- `extra.missingUploadTime`: The index must give upload-time (PEP 700); an override of false lifts it for the package. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/docs/usage/lockfile.md#exclude-packages-newer-than-specific-date)
- `extra.lockedSettings`: pdm.lock keeps a content_hash of the whole [tool.pdm.resolution] table (PyProject.content_hash), or with canonical lock inputs (lock_inputs = true, since 2.28.1) the table itself (src/pdm/project/lockfile/freshness.py), so a change to any key in it, exclude-newer and only-binary included, makes the lockfile out of date. pdm lock --check and pdm install --check then exit with 1 ("Lockfile doesn't satisfy the project requirements"), pdm install without --check locks again first and pdm sync only warns (check_lockfile in src/pdm/cli/actions.py) until pdm lock runs again; with exclude-newer set, pdm lock resolves every package again (src/pdm/cli/commands/lock.py). [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/src/pdm/project/project_file.py)
- `extra.commandLine`: pdm add takes requirements as arguments and editable ones with -e; its options come from cli/options.py and the global ones (-c/--config, --pep582, -I, -n, --no-cache) from core.py. --venv and --pep582 take an optional value, so argparse takes the next word for it. PDM parses with argparse, which accepts abbreviated long options. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/src/pdm/cli/commands/add.py)
- `extra.registryOverrides`: pypi.url, the index PDM uses when pyproject.toml names no source called pypi, can be set with PDM_PYPI_URL (docs/usage/config.md); -c/--config and PDM_CONFIG_FILE name another configuration file, which may set any index. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/src/pdm/project/config.py)
- `extra.selection`: pdm add --pre/--prerelease allows pre-releases of the added packages to be pinned and --stable only stable versions (prerelease_option; commands/add.py sets req.prerelease). PDM_NO_BINARY and PDM_ONLY_BINARY are lists of packages separated by commas, :all: for every package, of which no wheel, or only wheels, are locked and installed (docs/usage/lockfile.md; environments/base.py, _setting_list). [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/src/pdm/cli/options.py)
- `extra.latestVersion`: Released on 2026-10-30. [↗](https://github.com/pdm-project/pdm/blob/2.29.5/CHANGELOG.md)

### Pipenv

- `cooldown.setting`: In the [pipenv] section of the Pipfile: the resolver considers only versions uploaded at least that many days ago. Pipenv computes a cutoff (now minus N days, UTC) and hands it to pip as uploaded-prior-to. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/docs/pipfile.md#cool-down-period)
- `cooldown.configFiles`: The [pipenv] section. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/docs/pipfile.md#pipenv-directives)
- `cooldown.unit`: A string in <int>d format, e.g. "30d"; any other form is rejected (pipenv/vendor/plette/models/sections.py). [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/docs/pipfile.md#cool-down-period)
- `cooldown.availableSince`: "Added support for cool-down-period in the [pipenv] section of the Pipfile" under 2026.6.2 (repeated under 2026.7.0 and 2026.7.1). Checked against the wheels on 2026-10-30: missing in 2026.6.1, present in 2026.6.2. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/CHANGELOG.md)
- `cooldown.default`: Off unless set. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/docs/pipfile.md#cool-down-period)
- `installScripts.defaultPolicy`: Pipenv installs with pip, which builds source distributions when no wheel fits. Pipenv honors pip configuration and PIP_* variables, which may forbid building (PIP_ONLY_BINARY=:all:), but the Pipfile has no setting for it. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/docs/configuration.md)
- `project.lockfiles`: JSON, generated next to the Pipfile. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/docs/pipfile.md#pipfilelock)
- `project.manifests`: TOML. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/docs/pipfile.md#pipfile)
- `user.files`: Pipenv has no user configuration file of its own: it reads environment variables (set in a shell profile), the project .env file and pip configuration; pipenv/environments.py looks up no file. Since 2026.3.0 the pip install step runs with PIP_CONFIG_FILE=/dev/null (pipenv/utils/pip.py; CHANGELOG.md, #6066), so a user pip.conf no longer protects pipenv install and sync. The lock resolver still reads pip.conf, but only [global], because its pip command is named InstallCommand (pipenv/utils/resolver.py), and a Pipfile cool-down-period replaces its uploaded-prior-to. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/docs/configuration.md)
- `user.settings`: No user file to write to; at user level only PIP_* variables reach the pip install step (see variables). [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/docs/configuration.md)
- `user.unknownKeys`: No user file. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/docs/configuration.md)
- `user.invalidValueFails`: No user file. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/docs/configuration.md)
- `user.weakening`: No user file; see variables. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/docs/configuration.md)
- `extra.pylockCreatedBy`: Pipenv writes created-by = "pipenv" in the pylock.toml it generates (docs/pylock.md). pipenv install -e . writes the project itself as { path = ".", editable = true } (docs/pipfile.md), and Pipfile.lock keeps it as "path": ".". [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/pipenv/utils/pylock.py)
- `extra.configTables`: Directives such as cool-down-period and allow_prereleases live in [pipenv]. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/docs/pipfile.md#pipenv-directives)
- `extra.durationStrings`: Only whole days (<int>d) are accepted. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/docs/pipfile.md#cool-down-period)
- `extra.durationUnits`: Whole days only. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/docs/pipfile.md#cool-down-period)
- `extra.missingUploadTime`: "When the index does not provide upload-time metadata (e.g. most private mirrors) the setting is accepted but has no filtering effect." [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/docs/pipfile.md#cool-down-period)
- `extra.lockfileFormat`: Every key but _meta is a category (default, develop and custom ones) mapping names to entries: index packages have version, hashes and index; git entries git and ref; remote archives file; local projects path, and editable = true for editable installs (Pipfile "Packages Section"). The hashes of wheels and source distributions are listed together, so the lockfile does not show which packages are built. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/docs/pipfile.md#pipfilelock-structure)
- `extra.commandLine`: pipenv install takes packages as arguments (without any it installs the Pipfile) and editable ones with -e; -r imports a requirements file. The options of install and the global flags of pipenv, read with argparse, which accepts abbreviated long options. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/pipenv/cli/options.py)
- `extra.registryOverrides`: --index names a package index by URL or by a source name of the Pipfile; --pypi-mirror and PIPENV_PYPI_MIRROR replace PyPI. --extra-pip-args hands arguments to pip, which may name another index, and Pipenv loads PIP_* variables from the .env file that PIPENV_DOTENV_LOCATION names (options.py). [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/docs/configuration.md)
- `extra.selection`: pipenv install --pre allows pre-releases (and records allow_prereleases in the Pipfile, routines/install.py). Pipenv installs with pip, which reads PIP_NO_BINARY and PIP_ONLY_BINARY like --no-binary and --only-binary (see buildSwitch). [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/pipenv/cli/options.py)
- `extra.latestVersion`: Released on 2026-10-28. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/CHANGELOG.md)

### Renovate

- `cooldown.setting`: Formerly stabilityDays; old configs are migrated to "N days". Can be scoped with packageRules, vulnerabilityAlerts and update types. [↗](https://docs.renovatebot.com/configuration-options/#minimumreleaseage)
- `cooldown.configFiles`: Searched in this order. The "renovate" key in package.json still works but is deprecated. Shared presets (extends) can also set it. [↗](https://docs.renovatebot.com/configuration-options/)
- `cooldown.cliFlag`: Self-hosted CLI only; environment variable RENOVATE_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE. [↗](https://docs.renovatebot.com/configuration-options/#minimumreleaseage)
- `cooldown.unit`: For example "3 days" or "14 days". Since 42.19.5 "0 days" is treated like null. [↗](https://docs.renovatebot.com/key-concepts/minimum-release-age/)
- `cooldown.availableSince`: Earlier versions had the same feature as stabilityDays (first version not tracked). [↗](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/releases/tag/35.46.0)
- `cooldown.default`: Off unless configured; the docs table shows no default. config:best-practices adds "3 days" for npm (see presets). Since 44.96.0 minimumReleaseAgeBuffer adds 30 minutes once a delay is set. [↗](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/blob/main/lib/config/options/index.ts)
- `cooldown.exclude.setting`: No dedicated exclusion list. [↗](https://docs.renovatebot.com/key-concepts/minimum-release-age/#how-do-i-opt-out-dependencies-from-minimum-release-age-checks)
- `cooldown.exclude.patternSyntax`: Glob and regex patterns since 38.0.0. [↗](https://docs.renovatebot.com/configuration-options/#matchpackagenames)
- `cooldown.securityUpdates`: The vulnerabilityAlerts defaults set minimumReleaseAge to null; a delay can still be set inside vulnerabilityAlerts. [↗](https://docs.renovatebot.com/key-concepts/minimum-release-age/#what-happens-to-security-updates)
- `installScripts.defaultPolicy`: Renovate disables package manager scripts when it updates lockfiles; the Mend-hosted app never runs them. [↗](https://docs.renovatebot.com/configuration-options/#ignorescripts)
- `installScripts.disableAll`: The default; the self-hosted global allowScripts also defaults to false. [↗](https://docs.renovatebot.com/configuration-options/#ignorescripts)
- `extra.durationStrings`: Values such as "3 days" or "1 hour", parsed by toMs (lib/util/pretty-time.ts). [↗](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/blob/main/docs/usage/key-concepts/minimum-release-age.md)
- `extra.minimumReleaseAgePresets`: config:best-practices extends security:minimumReleaseAgeNpm, which sets minimumReleaseAge "3 days" for the npm datasource (see presets). [↗](https://docs.renovatebot.com/presets-security/#securityminimumreleaseagenpm)
- `extra.excludeRule`: The documented opt-out: a packageRules entry with matchPackageNames and minimumReleaseAge: null. [↗](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/blob/main/docs/usage/key-concepts/minimum-release-age.md)
- `extra.securityUpdatesSetting`: The vulnerabilityAlerts default sets minimumReleaseAge to null, so security updates skip the delay unless a value is set there. [↗](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/blob/main/lib/config/options/index.ts)
- `extra.excludeWildcards`: matchPackageNames accepts globs (and regex) since 38.0.0. [↗](https://docs.renovatebot.com/configuration-options/#matchpackagenames)
- `extra.ruleDescription`: A human-readable description allowed inside any configuration object; depcurfew uses it to recognize the packageRules entry it manages. [↗](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/blob/main/docs/usage/configuration-options.md#description)
- `extra.packageJsonConfig`: Deprecated: the configuration options page warns that support may be removed, and Renovate logs that using package.json is deprecated. [↗](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/blob/main/lib/workers/repository/init/merge.ts)
- `extra.durationUnits`: Units shown in the docs: minimumReleaseAge=1 hour on this page and "3 days" in the configuration options. The value is parsed by toMs (lib/util/pretty-time.ts), whose tests also accept 1 day, 1 week and combined values. [↗](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/blob/main/docs/usage/key-concepts/minimum-release-age.md)
- `extra.datasources`: Datasource ids for matchDatasources: npm packages come from the npm datasource and Python packages from pypi, whose release timestamp is the earliest upload_time of the version's files. [↗](https://docs.renovatebot.com/modules/datasource/pypi/)
- `extra.negativeMatch`: Patterns starting with ! are negative matches, and none of them may match; matchDatasources is matched this way (matchRegexOrGlobList in lib/util/package-rules/datasources.ts at 44.198.0), so ["!pypi"] covers every datasource but PyPI. [↗](https://docs.renovatebot.com/string-pattern-matching/)
- `extra.packageRuleMatching`: A packageRules entry applies to a dependency when all of its matchers match. Within one matcher, at least one positive pattern must match when there are any, and no negative pattern (starting with !) may match, so a list of only negative patterns matches every name it does not exclude (docs/usage/string-pattern-matching.md and matchRegexOrGlobList in lib/util/string-match.ts). matchPackageNames, matchDepNames, matchDatasources and matchUpdateTypes all match this way; "*" alone matches everything. [↗](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/blob/44.198.2/docs/usage/configuration-options.md#packagerules)
- `extra.packageRulesOrder`: All packageRules are evaluated and later rules override options set by earlier ones; a matching rule overrides the top-level configuration ("Package rule config overrides any existing config", lib/util/package-rules/index.ts). Presets in extends are merged before the repository configuration, and packageRules is mergeable, so the rules of presets come first and the repository's rules after them, while a top-level option of the repository replaces the same option of a preset (resolveConfigPresets in lib/config/presets/index.ts and mergeChildConfig in lib/config/utils.ts). [↗](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/blob/44.198.2/docs/usage/configuration-options.md#packagerules)
- `extra.delayedUpdateTypes`: The update types that take minimumReleaseAge into account; digest and pinDigest only for some datasources, and pin, lockFileMaintenance, lockfileUpdate, rollback, bump and replacement not at all. [↗](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/blob/44.198.2/docs/usage/key-concepts/minimum-release-age.md#which-update-types-take-minimumreleaseage-into-account)
- `extra.internalPresets`: The built-in preset groups; a default preset is written :name or default:name. Other presets (github>, gitlab>, local>, npm packages and so on) are fetched from elsewhere. Among the built-in presets only the security:minimumReleaseAge* presets set minimumReleaseAge, each in a packageRules entry with matchDatasources for its datasource, and config:best-practices extends security:minimumReleaseAgeNpm (security.preset.ts and config.preset.ts in the same directory). [↗](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/blob/44.198.2/lib/config/presets/internal/index.ts)
- `extra.pypiPresets`: Added in 44.8.0; config:best-practices does not include it (it includes only security:minimumReleaseAgeNpm). [↗](https://docs.renovatebot.com/presets-security/#securityminimumreleaseagepypi)
- `extra.pythonManagers`: pep621 updates pyproject.toml with uv.lock (there is no uv manager) or pdm.lock; poetry updates pyproject.toml with poetry.lock; pipenv updates the Pipfile with Pipfile.lock; pip_requirements updates requirements files. pip-compile is off by default (lib/modules/manager/pep621/readme.md and pipenv/index.ts at 44.198.1). [↗](https://docs.renovatebot.com/modules/manager/pep621/)
- `extra.passesDelayToManager`: Since 44.34.0 Renovate passes POETRY_SOLVER_MIN_RELEASE_AGE (rounded up to whole days) to Poetry 2.4.0 and later. It does not pass the delay to uv or read exclude-newer. [↗](https://docs.renovatebot.com/key-concepts/minimum-release-age/)
- `extra.missingTimestamp`: minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour was added in 41.150.0; timestamp-optional still fails open. [↗](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/releases/tag/42.0.0)
- `extra.independentOfPackageManager`: Source code passes --before to npm only; pnpm, Yarn and Bun gates are not read. [↗](https://docs.renovatebot.com/key-concepts/minimum-release-age/)

### Dependabot

- `cooldown.setting`: Per updates entry: default-days, semver-major-days, semver-minor-days, semver-patch-days, include, exclude. The semver-* keys apply only to SemVer ecosystems. [↗](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/supply-chain-security/dependabot-options-reference#cooldown)
- `cooldown.configFiles`: On the default branch. [↗](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/supply-chain-security/about-the-dependabot-yml-file)
- `cooldown.unit`: Integer days; the allowed range is disputed (see dayRange). [↗](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/supply-chain-security/dependabot-options-reference#cooldown)
- `cooldown.availableSince`: GA date on github.com; NuGet and Helm since 2025-07-29. [↗](https://github.blog/changelog/2025-07-01-dependabot-supports-configuration-of-a-minimum-package-age/)
- `cooldown.default`: Version updates wait 3 days even without a cooldown block (GHES from 3.23); default-days is also 3 when cooldown is set without it. [↗](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-07-14-dependabot-version-updates-introduce-default-package-cooldown/)
- `cooldown.securityUpdates`: Cooldown exists only for version updates. dependabot-core also passes a zero age to npm, pnpm and Yarn for security updates, overriding repository gates. [↗](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/supply-chain-security/dependabot-options-reference#cooldown)
- `installScripts.allowList.setting`: insecure-external-code-execution: allow exists only for bundler, mix and pip; nothing allows npm, pnpm, Yarn or Bun scripts. [↗](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/supply-chain-security/dependabot-options-reference#insecure-external-code-execution)
- `extra.cooldownKeys`: Keys inside the cooldown block of an updates entry; the semver-* keys override default-days for that kind of update. [↗](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/supply-chain-security/dependabot-options-reference#cooldown)
- `extra.excludeWildcards`: cooldown.exclude accepts * wildcards. [↗](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/supply-chain-security/dependabot-options-reference#cooldown)
- `extra.cooldownInclude`: An include list in the cooldown block limits the cooldown to the dependencies it names (* wildcards, up to 150 entries): the example applies the cooldown to requests, numpy and names starting with pandas or django, and to cover all dependencies one omits include or uses "*". The other dependencies get no cooldown at all, not even the default 3 days: dependabot-core skips the cooldown for a dependency that the include list does not match (ReleaseCooldownOptions#included? with File.fnmatch? and CooldownCalculation.skip_cooldown? in common/lib/dependabot, commit 03892a3e8ee26d43eb96f31c5136c98a85d63b14). exclude wins over include. [↗](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/tutorials/secure-your-dependencies/optimizing-pr-creation-version-updates#setting-up-a-cooldown-period-for-dependency-updates)
- `extra.ecosystems`: The npm ecosystem covers npm, pnpm and Yarn; bun needs Bun 1.1.39 or later and deno needs Deno 2. pip covers pip, pip-compile, pipenv and Poetry (v2); uv has its own ecosystem (the table lists uv v0.11). Cooldown, including the semver-* keys, is supported for all of them. PDM is not listed: dependabot-core skips the dependencies of pyproject.toml when pdm.lock exists (python/lib/dependabot/python/file_parser/pyproject_files_parser.rb at v0.402.0). [↗](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/supply-chain-security/dependabot-options-reference#package-ecosystem)
- `extra.maximumDays`: The page says the number of cooldown days must be between 1 and 90; whether 0 is accepted is disputed (see dayRange). [↗](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/tutorials/secure-your-dependencies/optimizing-pr-creation-version-updates)

### Environment

- `corepack.packageManagerField`: Format name@x.y.z, optionally followed by +<hash algorithm>.<hash>; a URL to a .js or .tgz file is also allowed. setup-bun also reads bun@x from this key. [↗](https://github.com/nodejs/corepack/blob/main/README.md)
- `corepack.devEnginesSince`: Limited support at first; since 0.36.0 Corepack uses the devEngines.packageManager range when packageManager is missing. [↗](https://github.com/nodejs/corepack/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
- `corepack.envFileSince`: Corepack reads COREPACK_* keys from .corepack.env; since 0.36.0 only the closest file. COREPACK_ENV_FILE=0 turns it off. [↗](https://github.com/nodejs/corepack/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
- `corepack.bundledWithNode`: Node.js 25.0.0 stopped distributing Corepack; the Corepack README says it ships with Node.js from 14.19.0 up to (but not including) 25.0.0. [↗](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/main/doc/changelogs/CHANGELOG_V25.md)
- `devEngines`: Each entry is an object or a list of objects with name (required), version and onFail (warn, error by default, or ignore). Corepack and the setup actions read it too. [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/docs/lib/content/configuring-npm/package-json.md#devengines)
- `devEnginesSince`: npm version that introduced devEngines. [↗](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v10.9.0/CHANGELOG.md)
- `volta.manifest`: Also extends: a path to another JSON file with a volta key. pnpm support is experimental and needs VOLTA_FEATURE_PNPM=1. [↗](https://github.com/volta-cli/volta/blob/main/crates/volta-core/src/project/serial.rs)
- `volta.maintained`: The README says Volta is unmaintained and recommends migrating to mise. [↗](https://github.com/volta-cli/volta/blob/main/README.md)
- `asdf.toolVersionsFile`: One tool per line followed by one or more versions separated by spaces (fallbacks); # starts a comment. [↗](https://github.com/asdf-vm/asdf/blob/master/docs/manage/configuration.md)
- `asdf.plugins`: Short names in the asdf plugin index; there is no plugin named node. python, uv and poetry checked on 2026-10-30 (danhper/asdf-python, asdf-community/asdf-uv, asdf-community/asdf-poetry). [↗](https://github.com/asdf-vm/asdf-plugins/tree/master/plugins)
- `githubActions.setupNode`: Current major v7. node-version-file reads package.json, .nvmrc, .node-version, .tool-versions or mise.toml; node-version wins when both are set. [↗](https://github.com/actions/setup-node/blob/main/action.yml)
- `githubActions.pnpmActionSetup`: Current major v6. Without version the action reads devEngines.packageManager or packageManager from package.json (package_json_file). [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/action-setup/blob/master/action.yml)
- `githubActions.pnpmSetup`: For pnpm 11 and later. Without version it reads devEngines.packageManager or packageManager; runtime takes <name>@<version> for node, bun or deno. [↗](https://github.com/pnpm/setup/blob/main/action.yml)
- `githubActions.setupBun`: Current major v2. Without bun-version it reads packageManager (bun@x), then engines.bun, then installs latest. [↗](https://github.com/oven-sh/setup-bun/blob/main/action.yml)
- `githubActions.setupDeno`: Current major v2. deno-version defaults to 2.x; deno-version-file reads .dvmrc or .tool-versions. [↗](https://github.com/denoland/setup-deno/blob/main/action.yml)
- `githubActions.setupPython`: Current version v7.1.0. Without python-version it reads .python-version; python-version wins over python-version-file. pip-version (major[.minor][.patch], CPython only) since v6.0.0. Python comes with pip, but the step alone does not show that pip installs the project. [↗](https://github.com/actions/setup-python/blob/v7.1.0/action.yml)
- `githubActions.setupUv`: Current version v10.3.3, with no moving v10 tag. Without version or version-file it reads required-version from uv.toml, then pyproject.toml, in the working directory, and installs the latest uv when neither has one. [↗](https://github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/blob/v10.3.3/action.yml)
- `githubActions.installPoetry`: A third-party action (current v1.4.2); version defaults to latest, so without it the Poetry version is not pinned. [↗](https://github.com/snok/install-poetry/blob/v1.4.2/action.yml)
- `githubActions.actionsPoetry`: A third-party action (current v4.0.0); poetry-version defaults to latest. [↗](https://github.com/abatilo/actions-poetry/blob/v4.0.0/action.yml)
- `githubActions.codeScanningUpload`: The example workflow on this page needs security-events: write in every repository and actions: read with contents: read only in private ones. The inputs come from upload-sarif/action.yml in github/codeql-action (current major v4, v4.39.1 checked); category tells analyses of the same tool and commit apart. [↗](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/how-tos/find-and-fix-code-vulnerabilities/integrate-with-existing-tools/upload-sarif-file)
- `githubActions.stopCommands`: Lines between the two are logged without being processed as workflow commands. The token must be randomly generated and unique for each run. Read from the page source in github/docs. [↗](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-commands#stopping-and-starting-workflow-commands)
- `githubActions.annotations`: escapeData and escapeProperty in @actions/core: the message and property values replace %, CR and LF; property values also replace : and , because properties are separated by commas. The commands and their file, line and title parameters are on https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-commands (line counts from 1). [↗](https://github.com/actions/toolkit/blob/main/packages/core/src/command.ts)
- `githubActions.annotationLimits`: 10 error, 10 warning and 10 notice annotations per step; 50 annotations per job, summed over all steps. Annotations over the limit are not shown. [↗](https://github.com/actions/toolkit/blob/main/docs/problem-matchers.md#limitations)
- `githubActions.stepSummary`: GitHub flavored Markdown appended to the file named by the variable; at most 1 MiB per step (over that the upload fails with an error annotation), and at most 20 step summaries are shown per job. [↗](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-commands#adding-a-job-summary)
- `npmRegistry.api`: GET /{package} returns the full document by default: dist-tags maps tags to versions (every package has latest), versions maps versions to version objects, time maps every version to its publish time, and a version object carries scripts (from its package.json) and deprecated. The abbreviated document (Accept: application/vnd.npm.install-v1+json) has no time field and adds hasInstallScript. Scoped names are escaped with %2f (escapedName in github.com/npm/npm-package-arg); the registry answered the same document for @types/node and @types%2fnode on 2026-10-29. Install scripts: preinstall, install and postinstall run for a dependency, and npm runs node-gyp rebuild as install when the package has binding.gyp and no install or preinstall script (github.com/npm/cli/blob/v12.2.1/docs/lib/content/using-npm/scripts.md); binding.gyp is not visible in the document. [↗](https://github.com/npm/registry/blob/main/docs/responses/package-metadata.md)
- `pypiIndex.api`: GET /simple/<project>/ with Accept: application/vnd.pypi.simple.v1+json returns name, files, meta, versions and project-status; the project is matched case-insensitively with _, - and . considered equal (index-api.md in pypi/warehouse, the source of docs.pypi.org/api/index-api/, which recommends the JSON form for new integrations; the JSON API of /pypi/<project>/json marks its releases key deprecated). A file has filename, url, hashes, size, an optional upload-time (yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.ffffffZ, UTC) and an optional yanked (true or a reason string). Every file belongs to a version listed in versions, but the response does not say which: the version is part of the file name. On 2026-10-30 pypi.org answered api-version 1.4 for requests and 404 for a name it does not know. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/packaging.python.org/blob/6fa4790c1fb668830f6eb94bbfe832320a9b0a2b/source/specifications/simple-repository-api.rst)
- `pypiIndex.projectStatus`: A project has exactly one status, active when none is given. quarantined: considered generally unsafe (for example malware), and the index must not offer any of its files. archived: no new uploads, existing files stay; installers may warn. deprecated: obsolete, perhaps superseded by another project; installers may warn. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/packaging.python.org/blob/6fa4790c1fb668830f6eb94bbfe832320a9b0a2b/source/specifications/project-status-markers.rst)
- `claudeCode.hooks`: A PreToolUse command hook gets the event as JSON on stdin and decides by printing one JSON object and exiting 0: deny prevents the call and shows the reason to Claude, ask prompts the user (also in auto mode), deny wins over ask. The PowerShell tool passes its command in tool_input.command with the same fields as the Bash tool. A matcher of names separated by | matches each of them exactly. With args set, command runs as an executable without a shell; on Windows it must resolve to a real executable such as a .exe, not a .cmd or .bat shim from node_modules/.bin. Without onFailure, a hook that fails to start, crashes or times out lets the call through. The if filter is best-effort; the docs recommend the permission system for hard allow or deny rules. [↗](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks)
- `claudeCode.shellTools`: Tool names are the exact strings of hook matchers. Bash executes shell commands. PowerShell executes PowerShell commands natively; hooks get its command in tool_input.command with the same fields as Bash, and the docs say to match Bash|PowerShell in hooks that inspect shell commands: on Windows, wherever the PowerShell tool is enabled, Claude treats PowerShell as the primary shell, and without Git Bash it is enabled automatically and the Bash tool is not registered at all (also https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#powershell). On Windows with Git Bash it is on by default for claude.ai and Console accounts, CLAUDE_CODE_USE_POWERSHELL_TOOL=0 turns it off, and Claude Code runs pwsh.exe or else powershell.exe 5.1. Monitor runs a command in the background and feeds its output lines back to Claude, with the same permission rules as Bash; on Windows it is available only with Git Bash; a WebSocket watch takes a ws input in place of command. [↗](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference)
- `git.ignore`: git status and git add skip untracked files that match a pattern from a .gitignore in the same directory or a parent (deeper files override higher ones, and within one file the last matching pattern decides), then from $GIT_COMMON_DIR/info/exclude (.git/info/exclude outside linked worktrees), then from core.excludesFile. Files already tracked are not affected. Patterns: # comments, ! negation, a leading or middle / anchors the pattern to the directory of its .gitignore, a trailing / matches directories only, * and ? do not match /, **/, /** and /**/ match any number of directories; a file below an ignored directory cannot be re-included. The tracked files are the entries of $GIT_DIR/index (Documentation/gitformat-index.adoc at v2.56.0: versions 2, 3 and 4). [↗](https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.56.0/Documentation/gitignore.adoc)
- `git.ignoreCase`: core.ignoreCase turns on workarounds for file systems that are not case sensitive (APFS, HFS+, FAT, NTFS); it defaults to false, but git clone and git init probe the file system and set it to true when appropriate, so a repository cloned on Windows or macOS has it. With it, git matches .gitignore patterns and looks up the index without regard to case: match_basename and match_pathname in dir.c compare with fspathncmp and fnmatch_icase_mem, which fold case (strncasecmp, WM_CASEFOLD) when repo_ignore_case is set, and environment.c reads core.ignorecase (both at v2.56.0). Section and variable names are case-insensitive, true is yes, on, true or 1 in any case, and a variable without = <value> is true (Documentation/config.adoc at v2.56.0). [↗](https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.56.0/Documentation/config/core.adoc)
- `windows.commandShims`: cmd-shim is "the cmd-shim used in npm to create executable scripts on Windows" (README): for each program of a package it writes <name>.cmd, which runs the program with %* (so cmd.exe reads the arguments again), <name>.ps1 for PowerShell and a sh script. npm ships the same files for itself: bin/npm.cmd, bin/npm.ps1, bin/npx.cmd and bin/npx.ps1 in github.com/npm/cli at v12.2.1, the .cmd files ending in "%NODE_EXE%" "%NPM_CLI_JS%" %*. [↗](https://github.com/npm/cmd-shim/blob/v9.0.2/lib/index.js)
- `windows.batchArguments`: about_Parsing (the source of https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.core/about/about_parsing): on Windows, arguments for batch files are passed as raw command-line strings to cmd.exe, and untrusted input should be passed another way. In the Windows mode of $PSNativeCommandArgumentPassing, the default on Windows since PowerShell 7.3, files ending in .bat or .cmd (also cmd.exe, cscript.exe, wscript.exe, .js, .vbs and .wsf) keep the legacy argument passing of Windows PowerShell 5.1. [↗](https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/PowerShell-Docs/blob/0061dc7f35abfa6bb5ffabaada1650163761f2e1/reference/7.5/Microsoft.PowerShell.Core/About/about_Parsing.md)
- `python.nameNormalization`: Names are lowercased and every run of ., - or _ becomes a single -, before lookups and comparisons (PEP 503): Friendly.Bard and friendly_bard are the same package. Read from the page source in pypa/packaging.python.org. [↗](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/name-normalization/)
- `python.namePattern`: The specification gives ^([A-Z0-9]|[A-Z0-9][A-Z0-9._-]*[A-Z0-9])\Z run with re.IGNORECASE (PEP 508). [↗](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/name-normalization/)
- `python.projectFile`: The configuration file of a Python project, in the project root; tools keep their own settings in its [tool.<name>] tables. [↗](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/pyproject-toml/)
- `python.wheelExtension`: A wheel is a ZIP archive with the .whl extension; installing it unpacks files and runs no build code. Read from the page source in pypa/packaging.python.org. [↗](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/binary-distribution-format/)
- `python.sourceDistributionExtensions`: ARCHIVE_EXTENSIONS of pip without .whl: the archives pip accepts from an index besides wheels (index/package_finder.py rejects any other extension), all of them built when installed. A standard sdist is named {name}-{version}.tar.gz with the name normalized (PEP 625, source-distribution-format.rst); older uploads use the other extensions and names that are not normalized. [↗](https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/src/pip/_internal/utils/filetypes.py)
- `python.hatch`: Hatch reads its project configuration from [tool.hatch] of pyproject.toml or from hatch.toml. It has no setting of its own for a release-age delay, building from source or dependency sources; its environments install with uv (installer = "uv", the default of its internal environments) or pip (docs/how-to/environment/select-installer.md), and uv reads [tool.uv] of the project under Hatch too (tested on 2026-10-30 with Hatch 1.18.2 and uv 0.13.6). [↗](https://github.com/pypa/hatch/blob/hatch-v1.18.2/docs/intro.md)
- `python.interpreter`: python [-bBdEhiIOPqRsSuvVWx?] [-c command | -m module-name | script | - ] [args]: -m and -c end the interpreter options, and what follows goes to the module or the command; -W arg, -X option and --check-hash-based-pycs mode take a value, the other options are flags. One-letter options may be grouped after one dash: _PyOS_GetOpt in Python/getopt.c (v3.14.0, SHORT_OPTS "bBc:dEhiIm:OPqRsStuvVW:xX:?") reads them one by one, and c, m, W and X take the rest of the word or the next word, so python3 -Im pip runs pip. pip documents running itself as python -m pip, and as py -m pip with the Windows launcher (github.com/pypa/pip/blob/26.2.2/docs/html/cli/pip_install.rst). [↗](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/v3.14.0/Doc/using/cmdline.rst)

## To review

Uncertain facts rest on incomplete official sources; disputed facts have official sources that disagree.

### npm · `installScripts.allowList.format` ❓ uncertain

The exact entry grammar (no semver ranges) is stated in accepted RFC 0054; the shipped docs describe entries only in prose.

- `Object keyed by name, name@version or name@v1 || v2 with true (allow) or false (deny); npm install-scripts approve writes pinned name@version entries` · [source](https://github.com/npm/rfcs/blob/main/accepted/0054-make-scripts-install-opt-in.md), verified 2026-10-28.

### npm · `sources.git.availableSince` ⚠️ disputed

The release notes add --allow-git in 11.9.0; the GitHub changelog says it was introduced in 11.10.0.

- Variant 1: `11.9.0` · [source](https://github.com/npm/cli/releases/tag/v11.9.0), verified 2026-10-28.
- Variant 2: `11.10.0` · [source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-05-22-staged-publishing-and-new-install-time-controls-for-npm/), verified 2026-10-28.

### npm · `sources.remoteTarball.availableSince` ⚠️ disputed

The 11.14.0 release notes add the flag; the GitHub changelog dates it to 11.15.0, which also moved enforcement into the resolver. Treat 11.15.0 as the safe minimum.

- Variant 1: `11.14.0` · [source](https://github.com/npm/cli/releases/tag/v11.14.0), verified 2026-10-28.
- Variant 2: `11.15.0` · [source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-05-22-staged-publishing-and-new-install-time-controls-for-npm/), verified 2026-10-28.

### npm · `sources.file.availableSince` ⚠️ disputed

The 11.14.0 release notes add the flag; the GitHub changelog dates it to 11.15.0, which also moved enforcement into the resolver. Treat 11.15.0 as the safe minimum.

- Variant 1: `11.14.0` · [source](https://github.com/npm/cli/releases/tag/v11.14.0), verified 2026-10-28.

### Yarn (Berry) · `user.weakening` ❓ uncertain

Read from code (resolveRcFiles, the same since 4.0.0; not on yarnpkg.com, and no test was read): lists from every .yarnrc.yml are joined, so home entries add to a project's list unless the project uses the undocumented { onConflict: reset } form; objects such as npmScopes merge key by key; for single values the file closest to the project wins. Since 4.17.0 a scope listed in the home npmScopes only for its registry gets the default gate of 1d instead of the project's gate (perScopeGate). A .yarnrc.yml in any folder between the root and the project merges the same way.

- `{"key":"approvedGitRepositories","values":"any","effect":"approves these git repositories in every project, on top of the project's own list"}`, `{"key":"npmPreapprovedPackages","values":"any","effect":"exempts these packages from the age gate in every project, on top of the project's own list"}`, `{"key":"enableScripts","values":[true],"effect":"runs dependency build scripts in every project whose .yarnrc.yml does not set enableScripts"}`, `{"key":"npmMinimalAgeGate","values":[0],"effect":"turns the age gate off in every project whose .yarnrc.yml does not set it"}`, `{"key":"npmScopes.*.npmMinimalAgeGate","values":[0],"effect":"turns the age gate off for that scope in every project"}` · [source](https://github.com/yarnpkg/berry/blob/%40yarnpkg/cli/4.18.1/packages/yarnpkg-core/sources/configUtils.ts), verified 2026-10-31.

### Yarn (Berry) · `user.variables` ⚠️ disputed

The yarnrc docs say environment variables cannot set lists, but parseValue splits a string on commas for list settings, so by the code YARN_APPROVED_GIT_REPOSITORIES and YARN_NPM_PREAPPROVED_PACKAGES work. The safe choice is to treat both as effective.

- Variant 1: `{"name":"YARN_ENABLE_SCRIPTS","anyCase":true,"values":["true","1"],"effect":"runs dependency build scripts, whatever any .yarnrc.yml says"}`, `{"name":"YARN_NPM_MINIMAL_AGE_GATE","anyCase":true,"values":"any","effect":"replaces npmMinimalAgeGate from every .yarnrc.yml"}`, `{"name":"YARN_APPROVED_GIT_REPOSITORIES","anyCase":true,"values":"any","effect":"replaces approvedGitRepositories from every .yarnrc.yml (a comma-separated list)"}`, `{"name":"YARN_NPM_PREAPPROVED_PACKAGES","anyCase":true,"values":"any","effect":"replaces npmPreapprovedPackages from every .yarnrc.yml (a comma-separated list)"}` · [source](https://github.com/yarnpkg/berry/blob/%40yarnpkg/cli/4.18.1/packages/yarnpkg-core/sources/Configuration.ts), verified 2026-10-31. A variable starting with yarn_ in any case sets the camel-cased setting before the rc files are read, and they cannot change it (Configuration.find and use; YARN_IGNORE_SCRIPTS is ignored); a list setting takes a comma-separated string (parseValue); enableScripts accepts true or 1 (parseBoolean).
- Variant 2: `{"name":"YARN_ENABLE_SCRIPTS","anyCase":true,"values":["true","1"],"effect":"runs dependency build scripts, whatever any .yarnrc.yml says"}`, `{"name":"YARN_NPM_MINIMAL_AGE_GATE","anyCase":true,"values":"any","effect":"replaces npmMinimalAgeGate from every .yarnrc.yml"}` · [source](https://github.com/yarnpkg/berry/blob/%40yarnpkg/cli/4.18.1/packages/docusaurus/static/configuration/yarnrc.json), verified 2026-10-31. Most settings "can also be defined through environment variables (at least for the simpler ones; arrays and objects aren't supported yet)", and such values "will overwrite any that might have been defined in the RC files".

The docs give ~/Library/Application Support/pypoetry on macOS. - Variant 2: 2.0.0+: `{"format":"toml","locations":[{"platforms":["linux"],"directories":[{"from":{"env":"XDG_CONFIG_HOME"},"path":"pypoetry"},{"from":"home","path":".config/pypoetry"}],"file":"config.toml"},{"platforms":["darwin"],"directories":[{"from":{"env":"XDG_CONFIG_HOME"},"path":"pypoetry"},{"from":"home","path":"Library/Application Support/pypoetry"}],"file":"config.toml"},{"platforms":["win32"],"directories":[{"from":{"env":"APPDATA"},"path":"pypoetry"},{"from":"home","path":"AppData/Roaming/pypoetry"}],"file":"config.toml"}]}` · [source](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/2.5.1/src/poetry/locations.py), verified 2026-10-31. ### Pipenv · `user.variables` ❓ uncertain

PIPENV_RESOLVER is not documented. The code ranks it above the resolver key of the Pipfile ("CLI/caller > env > current project's Pipfile > default"), and the pure-python backend locked the newest versions despite cool-down-period when chosen in the Pipfile (extra.resolverBypass, tested on 2026-10-30); the variable itself was not tested. PIPENV_PYPI_MIRROR: "When the index does not provide upload-time metadata (e.g. most private mirrors) the setting is accepted but has no filtering effect" (docs/pipfile.md). PIP_* variables are merged over the environment of the pip subprocess (pipenv/utils/processes.py), so they still reach it while pip.conf does not; pipenv/routines/install.py also reads PIP_NO_BINARY.

- `{"name":"PIPENV_RESOLVER","values":["pure-python"],"effect":"selects the pure-python resolver, which ignores cool-down-period"}`, `{"name":"PIPENV_PYPI_MIRROR","values":"any","effect":"replaces PyPI; on a mirror without upload times cool-down-period has no effect"}`, `{"name":"PIP_ONLY_BINARY","values":"any","effect":"sets only-binary of the pip Pipenv installs with, which no pip.conf reaches since 2026.3.0"}`, `{"name":"PIP_NO_BINARY","values":"any","effect":"builds these packages from source when installing, and pipenv install records no_binary for a named package in the Pipfile"}` · [source](https://github.com/pypa/pipenv/blob/v2026.10.4/pipenv/utils/resolver.py), verified 2026-10-31.
